group: Who has borrowed by selling bonds
title: Which currencies the world borrows in by selling bonds abroad: international debt securities by currency, in US dollars

rows.name: Not assigned to a currency
rows.basis: the BIS world total minus every currency listed (our calculation)

source: Bank for International Settlements, international debt securities (WS_DEBT_SEC2_PUB 1.0), amounts outstanding, all currencies, US dollars, by currency of issue, quarterly from December 1962; the BIS's combined euro line (EU1, the ECU, the euro and the currencies it replaced) overlaps the euro and is left out
note: International debt securities are bonds and notes a borrower sells outside its home market, for example a dollar bond that a Brazilian company sells in London. Each amount is what is still owed, in US dollars at the BIS's rate, so a row can move with exchange rates without any borrowing or repaying. Each row is bonds sold in that currency, whatever the borrower's country. Currencies the euro replaced keep their own rows until they stop. Not assigned is the world total minus every currency the BIS lists: 0.30% of the total in the latest quarter. Source: Bank for International Settlements.
